conceptually cool and fun game, but it's only fun with bots which are piss easy and bug out half the time. citations.review_text:
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare (2012)

The game itself is great and a lot of fun to play, but you cannot get the achievements in offline mode. You can get Chivalry 2's achievements in offline mode, so why not this one as well? They ended online servers for this game but you can still play on private servers and such, and even then I won't bother because if you don't live in the EU and you have high ping, people kick you for it.

There is very little reason to get Chivalry 1 over 2, unless you want to lan it with friends or something. Rather get number 2.

5/10

Wanted to get back into playing the game but my level is bugged and can no longer progress. Tried different things but nothing so far has worked. Even with the low player count and no official servers I could have enjoyed it but now there is no point. If this is how they treat their old games I definitely won't be buying any other games from these developers.

After careful consideration and evaluation, we’ve made the decision that after 12 years of support the official servers for 2012’s Chivalry: Medieval Warfare and its DLC Chivalry: Deadliest Warrior, will be taken offline as of April 8th 2024. This decision was not made lightly, and we understand it may impact those dedicated players who wish to play one of their favorite games.

[u]Review based on 100% completion of the game.[/u]
[hr][/hr]
[h3]7/10 - Good medieval fighting game, but near-dead community. Buy at your own risk![/h3]


This game was a hell of a lot of fun even years after it came out. The game is typically easy to learn, hard to master. You have a couple of classes of medieval fighters to choose from, with outfits you can customize to your liking. Each class comes with their strengths and weaknesses related to armor and stamina and besides some shared weapons, they have unique weapons for the most part. Each weapon is unique and has 3 different stats, i.e. length, speed and damage. There are a couple of different swing techniques that each have different animations and wind-up times. 

The game becomes hard to master once you realize that the veterans of the game understand that you can manipulate where in the swing of your weapon you actually force the hit registration. By swiping your mouse you can hit at the start, middle or end of your swing, and with certain longer weapons you can actually curve around the defense of an unsuspecting defender. Coupled with ping differences and long windups and the amount of stamina that you have to carefully manage, it quickly becomes evident that to understand the depths of this game, you have to understand the swing times and lengths of each weapon to really stand a chance in a fight against a veteran of the game. The game also has a multitude of voicelines which make for some hilarious situations when other players reciprocate. 

The remaining community is fun and for the most part very helpful and that's a nice segue into the population of the game. This game is pretty much dead, you'll see a lot of the same people playing this game at this point and if you are new you are in for a rough time. Another problem I have with this game, albeit minor in comparison to the dwindling community still playing, is that due to ping differences, this game can feel clunky, or janky at times. Combat an…

404 in the main menu. 24.99 price tag. not dead but still selling 7.99 usd skins straight from the main menu to the sub hundred people that check in with the game.

big positives are the fact there are dedicated servers whatsoever so people can choose to play the game with other people in a manner that pleases them and bot support which gives basic gameplay modes along with a horde mode offline support as well. if you want to get wild there is also the workshop.

it would be real swell if they put the game down to like 10 bucks, seems like a sane price to me. I would say lower but they gotta make their money. current base price being more than half the price of something like arc raiders is pretty wild. like I get the approach of I know what I got and its worth this much forever and fair enough but it certainly loses value when you boot the thing up and one of the first things you see is some html error and the mouse cursor is all laggy cuz its rendering the mouse at a locked ue3 smoothed frame nonsense. one of the other things I liked about it is it might be the last implementation of the unreal engine vote menu that was so so good, at least in ut2k4, it feels like it has that same DNA. let me know in the comments if theres a later unreal engine game that features a robust yet minimalist UI for mode \ map and possibly mutator voting support. I also like the sounds in the game, lots of nonsense shouting to do which I reckon was probably at least half of the time spent doing between and even during fighting.

positive review comes when they can scrape the money enough to give the game a kick in the tush update to make the 404 error a nice picture of a lizard or something cool like a jet fighter and bring the price down to like 5 bucks or something we can meet in the middle on. or heck just raise the price if the strategy is to eliminate competing with yourself or making newer games look bad when this one has plenty of function

This is a great aracadey medieval PvP game that is a lot of fun.  Some people expect it to be Mordhau levels of sword play and think it’s less skill based.  Sweaties.  I found it to be a lot of fun and the sword play and fighting to be more arcade like and enjoyable.  There is some skill you can develop with parrying and feinting if you want to go deep in it.  The matches are a lot of fun and everyone seems to have a hoot and a laugh while playing.  It’s fun rushing in and chopping an enemies arm off while dodging arrows from the archers and having your character scream a war cry.    I was excited to see them make a sequel to this great medieval PvP multiplayer experience.  Chilvary is definitely a great game!  
If you are considering giving it a go, which I recommend, I say get the latest game in the series and the sequel to this one; Chilvary 2 as it expands on the fighting with more weapons, skins, maps, and game modes.  Definitely a lot of fun to be had.  I wanted to give this part one of the series its flowers, a thumbs up and positive review as I had a lot of fun matches and great playing experience.  I have since moved on to the sequel Chilvary 2 when it was released, but wanted to thumbs up where it all started. 

TLDR:  fun medieval multiplayer PvP experience, but get the latest release and sequel Chilvary 2 for more medieval mayhem!

citations.review_text:
Medieval swordfights: chaos, blood, and someone yelling “for Agatha!” way too loud.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is old‑school multiplayer melee combat where you charge, feint, parry, and wildly swing everything from broadswords to longbows in big team battles and siege objectives. Think medieval carnage with a dash of Monty Python and a lot of “why did I just get stabbed from behind?” vibes. 

Pros:

Classic PvP sword fights, siege maps, and objective modes ⚔️ 

Lots of weapons and artful chaos once you get the hang of it 🍗 

Very positive long‑term community love on Steam 💥 

Cons:

Hit detection and melee feel a bit floaty compared to newer games 😅 

No single‑player — pure multiplayer focus 🕹️ 

Official servers have shut down (community/ private servers are still a thing) ⚠️ 

Verdict:
Great chaotic medieval brawls for fans of hack‑and‑slash PvP — but expect old‑school charm and old‑school rough edges.
Recommended (especially on sale).

Only reason for the downvote is really only some of the animations, and of course servers have gone offline, but the game is slightly more historically accurate than mordhau, the customization limits kind of kept the game somewhat in line with that.

Leaving it to not recommended b/c it seems to be dying and there is no point buying it now (may as well play Mordhau or Chiv 2), not b/c it was a bad game.
Thanks for the fond memories.

citations.review_text: Might be hald dead,but its stil better than Mordhau.  And vs ai is still going strong if you want to experience rooms of forever spawning enemies.Thats still fun.

I totaly recommend chivalry! i just made a minecraft map inside chiv's map maker. the map software was easy-to-use with total customization of the lighting!

UPDATE: Chivalry 2 needs a map editor! I'm sorry, but, I won't be purchasing chiv2 because of the obvious lack of support. chivalry 1 still has a launcher to create and upload full custom maps + custom weapon/armor+mods directly to the steam workshop since 2014!!

2014 is only two years after the game released in 2012

BUT the chiv1 map support is limited to FFA/LTS and Large scale Team objective battles are more complicated to make. unless you are a Zed and create horde mode using simply the Team Objective gamemode kismet editor .... Chivalry uses a modified version of Unreal Engine 3, the engine used for Gears of War, Rainbow six Vegas, Etc. kismet language is the unreal engine 3 version of Blueprints in unreal 5.. you can see a stitched screenshot of my entire map code on my steam page and flicker album.

Chivalry allows you to open any map inside the editor to learn the language very quickly, which become massively large systems on the Team objective mode such as GreenTower that you'll need to zoom into to decipher. Anybody can open my golden apple duelyard, fly around and select the items you want to copy, paste them into a new world. and open the Green K (kismet symbol) to edit or change the code, and copy everything you see, and you won't need to learn the logic behind the golden apple healing function.

chivalry 1 already gives you a huge library of assets, but if you want to remake an official map in the cookedPC/AOC/Levels folder

there's a program called Umodel (u can google it)

it lets u extract cooked packages from unreal games into their uncooked version for editing and re-uploading under a new name

I love this game with all my heart.
Thanks to this game, I met a huge number of people of different nationalities and views on life.
I have made many friends and enemies, but even to my enemies I am grateful for
the experience they gave me in this game.
Some of these people, to my great regret, have already left this game for various reasons.
Of course, the game is not without its drawbacks: there is a high barrier to entry and a rather toxic community, but still there are a lot of good and cheerful people here and this is probably the only thing that keeps me in that game so far.

There are countless emotions this game has brought me: anger, joy and even sadness.

Deserved 10/10

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that combat involves unintended techniques and physics exploits, such as hitting opponents from behind or dragging attacks.

citations.review_text:
Broken combat (backhit), empty servers
Only nerds with 0 fun left
2/10

[h1]TLDR[/h1]
This game is very good if you enjoy PVP combat, it has slowly dwindled in playerbase though. I still encourage people to try it out for a unique experience and have some tips below.

[h1]At first glance[/h1]
The combat is very approachable and fun. You can dismember opponents and every successful attack feels good even after 450 hours. It has simple to understand mechanics:
[list]
[*] A few different attack anims (slash, stab, overhead) with alternate variations (keep clicking or hold alt to get them)
[*] Cancel anims to feint (most people think this is cringe and don't do it)
[*] Start a block anim with right click but time it wrong and you can get hit while you recover from the block anim
[*] Kick, (makes shields largely useless you are very good)
[*] Projectile ranged weapons that require timing and drop compensation
[/list]

This game is immediately fun.

[h1]Endless Depth[/h1]
But what kept me coming back for 450 hours was the unintended massive well of depth:
[list]
[*] Attacks can be sped up or slowed down by dragging your mouse with or against the direction of the attack
[*] Attacks can be timed differently based on your orientation when you start them
- This means you can turn your back to the enemy, look up, and do an overhead attack to hit them way faster
- You can start big swipes turning the start of the attack closer or further away from your enemy or fake them out by starting close, missing on purpose, and doing a spin
[*] There are endless mindgames to get your opponent to block when:
- You didn't actually attack (fake them out with movement or looking quickly or using the Man-At-Arms dash or jumping etc)
- Your attack takes longer than they expected (dragging the mouse against the attack direction)
[*] You can move the mouse in a specific away to speed up or slow down stab attacks (which can be very confusing)
[*] You can kick to interrupt the opponents attack to reset the exchange
[*] You can bait them to attack and move just out of r…

I thought for a long time about what rating to give, I decided that it was a thumbs up, but the game is just a cactus that falls out of your ass, just a bunch of fresh ♥♥♥♥ in the village, after the shepherd passed by and you stepped on it. And all because in the game there are brainless nerds who play it 24/7 and you need to kill them for achievements, they do not provide any enlightenment and spoil the whole experience.
Servers with low levels don’t work, because only the same nerds play this game on the same server, with the same nicknames... But there is a slice of pleasure when you cut off his head and go call him a noob in the chat, his ass burns instantly and they offer 1x1.
While I was writing this review, I realized that the finger would still be down, I remembered the attacks that can be done from behind, the developers apparently could not fix this and said that this was a feature of the game. No - this is unrealistic diarrhea. The music and sounds are very good. Your body is some kind of clumsy mechanism, it doesn’t taste good. The levels are very good and it’s interesting to see everything.
